correctness.rationale: For either pure spherical-cap branch, every curvature equals 1/R. A mixed two-sphere fiber yields h=(f1+f2)/2+constant. Direct differentiation yields -D2fi=(Wi/R)(I+pi piT), and restriction to v perpendicular to p1-p2 yields exactly II(v,v)=[(W1+W2)/(2RW)] I(v,v). Strict midpoint convexity of sqrt(1+|p|²) proves the threshold and equality cases. The hyperplane has dimension n-2, so inertia gives at most one sub-threshold principal eigenvalue. At C2 seams and vertical-tangent regular points, shape-operator continuity closes the inequality. The known published 3D lens has a deficient curvature, proving sharpness, and the lower direction embeds in higher dimensions. Finite numeric verification reproducibly checks examples but is not a universal proof.

value.rationale: Steiner symmetrization can destroy ball-body curvature in dimensions at least three, creating a structural question about how many independent curvature directions are affected. This theorem sharply shows that every two-ball lens loses the threshold in at most one of n-1 directions while the other n-2 directions obey an explicit gain factor; the restriction is optimal in every dimension. The pointwise rank classification and quantitative transverse identity add structure not implied by simply knowing one counterexample or curvature failure magnitude.
